title: Cloud Essentials
subtitle: Guess the hidden cloud terms — spin for consonants, buy vowels

puzzles.hint: Cloud model where the provider delivers virtualized compute, storage, and networking — you manage the OS up
puzzles.explain: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) gives organizations on-demand access to raw virtualized infrastructure over the internet. The cloud provider owns and maintains the physical hardware while the customer controls operating systems, middleware, and applications.

puzzles.hint: Framework that divides security duties between the cloud provider and the customer
puzzles.explain: The shared responsibility model defines which security tasks belong to the cloud provider and which belong to the customer, and the exact split shifts depending on the service model (IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS). Understanding this boundary is foundational to designing a secure cloud environment.

puzzles.hint: A logically isolated network partition inside a public cloud provider's infrastructure
puzzles.explain: A Virtual Private Cloud is a private, isolated section of a public cloud where customers can define their own IP address ranges, subnets, route tables, and gateways. It gives organizations the network control of a private data center while retaining the scale and flexibility of public cloud.

puzzles.hint: Practice of provisioning and managing cloud resources through machine-readable configuration files instead of manual clicks
puzzles.explain: Infrastructure as Code allows teams to define servers, networks, and services in version-controlled scripts or templates, enabling repeatable and auditable deployments. Tools such as Terraform and AWS CloudFormation are common implementations of this practice.

puzzles.hint: Flat storage architecture that saves data as discrete objects — each with metadata and a unique identifier
puzzles.explain: Object storage manages data as self-contained units called objects rather than files in a hierarchy or blocks on a disk, making it highly scalable for unstructured data such as images, backups, and logs. Amazon S3 and Azure Blob Storage are well-known examples of this model.

puzzles.hint: The maximum acceptable length of time a system can be offline after a failure
puzzles.explain: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) defines how quickly a business must restore a service or process after a disruption before the downtime causes unacceptable damage. A lower RTO requires more redundant infrastructure and typically increases cost.

puzzles.hint: Cloud pricing model where you are billed only for the resources you actually consume
puzzles.explain: Pay as you go eliminates large upfront capital expenditure by charging customers based on actual usage — compute hours, storage gigabytes, or data transferred. This model aligns cost directly with demand and is one of the core economic advantages of public cloud.

puzzles.hint: Cloud security framework for controlling who can authenticate and what actions they are authorized to perform
puzzles.explain: Identity and Access Management (IAM) lets organizations define users, groups, roles, and policies that govern access to cloud resources. Properly configured IAM is considered the first line of defense in cloud security, enforcing the principle of least privilege.
